description: Drop into ply 20 of a real MCTS vs MCTS Fleet Draft match. Run the five-question scan live against orthogonal and diagonal Heavy-wing pressure. Generated from engine play (seed 9200).

scenes.eyebrow: Fleet Academy · Episode 9 · Live vs AI
scenes.headline: Practical AI Skirmish
scenes.subhead: Fleet Draft midgame — MCTS vs MCTS. Show the scan, don’t recite it.
scenes.voiceover: Episode nine: a practical AI skirmish. No textbook opening — we drop into a live Fleet Draft midgame generated by the engine’s own MCTS captains, and we run the five-question scan under fire.

scenes.headline: The match you are joining
bullets: Join at ply 20 — Carriers and Refractors already moved
scenes.voiceover: This is not a scripted mission opening. Two MCTS agents played Fleet Draft from the first ply — Refractor and Hub-anchored Carrier on files three and seven. We cut in at ply twenty, after both Carriers have stepped and a Refractor has contested the midboard. White to move. Treat the AI as ruthless.

scenes.caption: Opening → ply 20 (Fleet Draft)
scenes.voiceover: Watch the Heavy wing leave home rank. Carriers tether to Hubs; Refractors take diagonals. By ply twenty the board is a midgame — not a theory diagram.
Ply twenty. Black’s Hub has marched to six-six. Coverage is contested. Pause the board in your head and run the scan before you touch a piece.

scenes.headline: Five-question scan — live
bullets: 1 · Can I take their Hub this ply?
2 · Can they take mine after my move?
3 · What does this do for the nets?
4 · Files — and diagonals (Fleet Draft is live)
5 · Am I overextending into enemy glow?
scenes.voiceover: Same five questions as Episode one, now with Heavy geometry. Can you take their Hub? After your move, can they take yours — if yes, the Hub is hanging; refuse that candidate. What does the move do for the nets? Check Beam files and Refractor diagonals. Finally: are you stepping into their Sensor Net just to look busy?

scenes.prompt: White to move at ply 20. Which threats matter first — Hub safety, net growth, or Heavy geometry?
scenes.voiceover: Pause and predict. The AI will keep squeezing coverage and Carrier lanes. Name the first threat you refuse before you chase a flashy diagonal.
scenes.revealVoiceover: Eight plies later the lattice is still tense — legal replies stay high, Hubs still alive. Good captains dismantle orthogonal and diagonal pressure without leaving the flagship where it can be captured next turn. That is the skirmish habit: scan, keep the Hub safe, then trade.

scenes.voiceover: Ply twenty-eight. Contested Space is purple — it feeds neither Integration Hold. Against Fleet Draft, paint purple into Carrier and Refractor glow the same way you would against Beams. Diagonal slides do not get a free pass.

Ply forty — end of this teaching cut. A White Infiltrator sits Target Locked deep in Black’s net. Locks erase Heavy slides too: a locked Carrier crawls. You just practiced the scan against real AI branching. Next episode: the piece we keep saving for “real targets.”

scenes.headline: Scan under fire
scenes.voiceover: That is the practical skirmish: Fleet Draft, real MCTS play, five questions under pressure. Next: Phase Runners — how an Infiltrator warps, and how Target Lock kills the fold.
